description: Extends the shared preset at yschimke/renovate-config, which owns the release-train grouping for the ee.schimke.composeai group. platformAutomerge lets native GitHub auto-merge land minor/patch/digest/pin bumps once every required check is green. The packageRules below are this repository's own floors and ceilings: what renderer-android and the published `data-*` connectors are compiled against is part of their supported-minimum surface, so a green build is not on its own a reason to take an upgrade (docs/RENDERER_COMPATIBILITY.md). There is no `schedule`: neither this file nor the preset sets one, so an update is proposed on whichever Renovate run first sees it (roughly hourly on the hosted app). Third-party dependencies still soak for the 7-day `minimumReleaseAge` below; the first-party contracts and rc-players BOMs opt out of it and arrive as soon as they are published.

github-actions.description: Every `uses:` in this repository is SHA-pinned with a `# vX.Y.Z` comment, so with the manager off the pins could never move and a fixed action would never reach CI. Renovate rewrites the digest and the version comment together, and `pinDigests` keeps a newly added tag-only `uses:` from staying unpinned.

packageRules.description: Never take a `…-compat` backport artifact. JetBrains publishes compatibility variants of the kotlinx libraries under a `<version>-<oldline>.x-compat` suffix (e.g. `kotlinx-datetime:0.8.0-0.6.x-compat`, the 0.8.0 code recompiled against the 0.6.x API) and Renovate's gradle versioning ranks that suffix ABOVE the plain release, so it proposes a *downgrade of API surface* dressed as an upgrade (#3359). Filtering the suffix out of the candidate list — rather than disabling the update — keeps Renovate offering the next genuine release. Declared before the per-dep pins below so those stricter `allowedVersions` still win for their deps. Also carries the `-SNAPSHOT` filter the shared preset applies across the gradle manager: both rules set `allowedVersions` and the last match wins, so naming only `-compat` here would hand every Gradle dependency in this repository its snapshots back (Renovate ranks `1.0.0-SNAPSHOT` above `1.0.0-alpha18`).

Hold ClassGraph below 6. 6.0.0 is compiled for Java 25 (class file 69), so on this repository's JDK 17 floor every scan fails with UnsupportedClassVersionError. (5.x keeps class file 61; it is 5.0 that removed the 4.x API, `overrideClasspath`, `getAnnotationInfo`, `typeDescriptorStr`, so a 5.x bump is a port that must land with compose-ai-tools and compose-preview-server, never a version-only Renovate merge.) The shared preset carries the same cap, but the gradle-wide `-compat` rule just above also sets `allowedVersions` and comes later, so it overrides the preset's ClassGraph rule (last match wins); this rule restores the cap. It names plain `x.y.z` releases, which also keeps out `-compat` and `-SNAPSHOT`; Renovate's RE2 regexes have no lookahead to exclude them otherwise. Lift it only together with a Java 25 floor and a ported discovery.

compose-bom-compat: pin to the 2025.11.x line (compose-ui 1.9.5) — renderer-android's published bytecode targets the oldest supported Compose. Renovate must not drift this floor higher; bumping the supported-Compose-minimum is a manual decision.

material-kolor: pin to the 4.0.x line. `:data-wallpaper-connector` is published against the renderer-android Compose floor (`compose-bom-compat`, Compose 1.9.5); 4.1.0 rebuilt against Compose Multiplatform 1.10.0 + Kotlin 2.3.0 and migrated to a Multiplatform Android library, raising the transitive floor above our published surface. See gradle/libs.versions.toml for the full rationale — bumping the floor is a manual decision.

androidx.core:core: pin to the 1.13.x line. `:data-keyboard-connector` declares this as a `compileOnly` compat floor so the published AAR's bytecode stays binary-backward-compatible with consumers on older `androidx.core` lines (same rationale as `compose-foundation` via `compose-bom-compat`). Raising the floor is a manual decision.

Remote Compose, its Wear widget layer and Glance Wear resolve from Google Maven on released alpha coordinates, and the three groups only work together when built against the same `remote-creation*` — `remote-material3` and `androidx.glance.wear:*` name that version in their POMs. Renovate updates one dependency at a time, so an automated bump of any one group produces exactly the skew that has taken CI red before (a `NoClassDefFoundError` inside `RemoteButtonImpl` at render time, a wear pin that did not exist yet). Bump the three refs in gradle/libs.versions.toml as one set after checking the POMs, and re-verify a render, not just a compile.

One PR for the workflow pins rather than one per action: these land as a workflow-only change that the same required checks gate, and reviewing them together is how a bad action bump is spotted. Grouping is expressed as a packageRule because that is the stage at which Renovate builds branches.

eclipse-temurin 25 fails distribution/image/test-render-runtime-image.sh ('base must be FROM eclipse-temurin:21.0.13.1_2-jdk') because the render-runtime base image intentionally stays on Temurin 21 until a deliberate runtime/render validation moves it. Skipped from https://github.com/yschimke/compose-preview-daemon/pull/512. Remove or raise when migrating the render-runtime image to Java 25 and updating test-render-runtime-image.sh together.

customManagers.description: The `xr-composite` pin — the compositor's release version in compose-preview-xr. Invisible to the gradle manager: it is a bare `[versions]` entry with no library or plugin declaring `version.ref = "xr-composite"`, so there is no coordinate for Renovate to resolve. The CLI and the Gradle plugin both bake it in at build time and resolve the binary by it, so without this it is the one dependency here that could never be offered an update. Anchored to this single entry rather than written generically, because `extractVersionTemplate` below is specific to it: the catalog holds a bare `1.0.0` while the upstream tags are `v1.0.0`.
